story_description: As a user with multiple sessions, I need to know which background sessions have new events so I can prioritize which session to review next without manually checking each one.
task_description: Create the ReadStateStore actor that tracks last-read event sequence positions per session, calculates unread counts, and persists state to SQLite.
atom_description: Implement the ReadStateStore Swift actor with methods for tracking read positions, calculating unread counts, marking sessions as read, and persisting to the session_read_states SQLite table.
problem_statement: Users cannot tell if background worktrees or inactive sessions have received new events. Without unread tracking, users must manually check each session to discover new activity, which wastes time and creates cognitive load.
scope_in: Implement markAsRead(sessionId:sequence:) method to update read position
Implement loadAllReadStates() method for app startup
Implement persistReadState(sessionId:sequence:) method for SQLite writes
Add ReadState model struct with sessionId, lastReadSequence, and lastReadAt fields
scope_out: Real-time event subscription and count updates (covered in T002)
Read state export or backup functionality
assumptions: SQLite database connection is available via existing Database actor
Session IDs are stable UUID strings that persist across app restarts
Event sequences are monotonically increasing integers per session
The EventStore already tracks total event count per session
constraints: Must use Swift actor for thread-safe concurrent access
Must persist to SQLite for crash recovery
Read state updates must complete within 50ms to avoid UI lag
Must not block main thread during persistence operations
Must handle database migration from existing schema
functional_requirements: FR1: ReadStateStore.getLastReadSequence(sessionId:) returns the last read event sequence for a session, or 0 if never read
FR2: ReadStateStore.markAsRead(sessionId:sequence:) updates the read position and lastReadAt timestamp
FR4: ReadStateStore.loadAllReadStates() loads all persisted states into memory on app startup
FR5: Read state changes persist to SQLite within 1 second of the markAsRead call
FR6: ReadStateStore handles concurrent read and write operations safely via actor isolation
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Actor methods complete within 50ms for single-session operations
NFR2: loadAllReadStates completes within 200ms for up to 1000 sessions
NFR3: SQLite writes are batched if multiple updates occur within 100ms window
NFR4: Memory usage for cached read states stays under 1MB for 10000 sessions
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create Blaze/Sources/Data/ReadStateStore.swift with actor declaration and ReadState struct
Step 2: Add private dictionary readStates: [String: ReadState] for in-memory cache
Step 3: Implement init(database:) that takes Database actor dependency
Step 4: Implement loadAllReadStates() that queries session_read_states table and populates cache
Step 5: Implement getLastReadSequence(sessionId:) that returns cached value or 0
Step 6: Implement markAsRead(sessionId:sequence:) that updates cache and schedules persistence
Step 7: Implement getUnreadCount(sessionId:totalEvents:) with max(0, totalEvents - lastRead) calculation
Step 8: Implement persistReadState(sessionId:sequence:) with INSERT OR REPLACE SQL
Step 10: Register ReadStateStore in BlazeApp.swift dependency injection
data_model_changes: Add ReadState struct with fields: sessionId (String), lastReadSequence (Int64), lastReadAt (Date)
Add session_read_states table: session_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, last_read_sequence INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, last_read_at DATETIME NOT NULL
api_contracts: ReadStateStore.markAsRead(sessionId: String, sequence: Int64) async throws
ReadStateStore.getUnreadCount(sessionId: String, totalEvents: Int64) async -> Int
event_contracts: Internal: readStateUpdated(sessionId: String, newSequence: Int64) posted to NotificationCenter after markAsRead
No external event emission - UI observes via Combine publisher on ReadStateStore
ui_states: N/A - this atom is data layer only
ui_interactions: N/A - this atom is data layer only
ui_copy: N/A - this atom is data layer only
edge_cases: EC1: markAsRead called for non-existent session - create new ReadState entry
EC2: markAsRead called with sequence lower than current - ignore (keep higher value)
EC3: getUnreadCount called before loadAllReadStates completes - return 0 as safe default
EC4: Database locked during write - retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff
EC5: Session deleted while read state exists - orphan cleanup on next loadAllReadStates
EC6: App crash during persistence - incomplete write handled by SQLite transaction rollback
failure_modes: FM1: SQLite database corruption - log error, reset read states to empty, continue with in-memory only until restart
FM2: Out of memory loading states - implement pagination for loadAllReadStates if more than 10000 sessions
FM3: Actor deadlock - use nonisolated methods for read-only operations where safe
rollback_plan: Revert ReadStateStore.swift creation and Migration.v7 changes. Run migration rollback SQL: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS session_read_states. Remove ReadStateStore registration from BlazeApp.swift.

acceptance_tests: AT1: Given a new session, when getLastReadSequence is called, then 0 is returned
AT2: Given markAsRead(sessionId, 10) was called, when getUnreadCount(sessionId, 15) is called, then 5 is returned
AT3: Given read states exist in SQLite, when app launches and loadAllReadStates completes, then cached values match database
AT4: Given concurrent markAsRead calls from multiple tasks, when all complete, then highest sequence wins
acceptance_criteria: AC1: ReadStateStore actor compiles without warnings
AC2: All unit tests pass with 100% coverage of public methods
AC3: Integration test proves persistence across app lifecycle
AC4: Performance tests confirm sub-50ms markAsRead latency
AC5: SQLite migration runs successfully on fresh and existing databases

Unit tests cover all public methods

completed_when: ReadStateStore actor is fully implemented, all tests pass, migration runs successfully, and performance benchmarks confirm sub-50ms latency for markAsRead operations.

open_questions: OQ1: Should read states be pruned when sessions are deleted, or allow orphan cleanup on next load?
OQ2: Should we batch multiple rapid markAsRead calls into a single SQLite write?
notes: This is the foundational atom for unread badge functionality. The ReadStateStore actor provides the data layer that S002-BADGE UI and T002 real-time updates will consume.

risks: R1: Actor isolation overhead may exceed 50ms target on older hardware
R2: SQLite write contention with SessionStore during high event volume
R3: Memory pressure from caching read states for many sessions
mitigations: M1: Use nonisolated read methods where thread-safe; benchmark on Intel Mac Mini
M2: Use separate SQLite connection or WAL mode for concurrent writes
M3: Implement LRU eviction for sessions not accessed in 24 hours
risk_register.blast_radius: Isolated to Data layer. No UI impact if ReadStateStore fails - badges simply show 0. SessionStore unaffected.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If ReadStateStore causes issues, disable by returning 0 from all getUnreadCount calls. Users lose unread tracking but app remains functional.

events: readStateUpdated notification posted after markAsRead completes
